§ 2Content

§ 3Indian Classical Music

  • Indian classical music is divided into two categories: Hindustani music and Carnatic music.
  1. 1. Hindustani Music (North India)
  • Sung in languages: Hindi, Braj, Awadhi, Rajasthani, Marathi.
  1. 2. Carnatic Music (South India)
  • Sung in languages: Sanskrit, Kannada, Telugu, Malayalam, Tamil.

Common Elements in Both Traditions

  1. 1. Raga: A melodic framework, each associated with a specific emotion or time of the day. E.g. Miyan ki Todi (sung during late morning hours).
  2. 2. Taal: A rhythmic framework based on cyclic time units.
  3. 3. Sruti: The smallest measurable difference between musical pitches.

7 Basic Swaras in Indian Music (Sargam)

  • Sa → Shadjam
  • Re → Rishabham
  • Ga → Gandharam
  • Ma → Madhyamam
  • Pa → Panchamam
  • Da → Dhaivatham
  • Ni → Nishadham

"Bhoop corresponds to the 'Mohanam Ragam' of carnatic music."

3 Major Vocal Forms of Hindustani Music

Dhrupad

  • It is sung with a Tanpura and Pankhawaj.
  • Dhrupad was first composed by Miyan Tansen.
  • It was propounded by Dagar family and Darbhanga Gharana.

Khayal

  • A more lyrical and expressive form that evolved from Dhrupad, known for its freedom of expression and romantic themes.
  • Khayal was first composed by Amir Khusrau.

Tarana

  • It is performed towards the end of concert.
  • It is used to convey the mood of elation.
  • Tillana of Carnatic music is based on this.

Lighter vocal forms in Hindustani classical music, often considered semi-classical, include Dhamar (associated with Dhrupad), Kajari, Tappa, Thumri, Ghazal, Bhajan, Tripal, and Chaiti.

Major Styles of Carnatic Music

  1. 1. Gitam: A simple melodic extension of the raga with a uniform tempo and introductory piece.
  2. 2. Svarajati: Mix of devotional and heroic elements. This is learnt after a course of Gitam.
  3. 3. Kirtanam: It comprises of devotional songs.
  4. 4. Tillana: Short, crisp compositions, similar to Tarana in Hindustani music.
  5. 5. Kriti: It comprises of highly evolved musical compositions. It is a development from Kirtana.
  6. 6. Suladi: An extension of raga-based compositions.
  7. 7. Padam: A love poem/tempo.

Important Personalities in Indian Classical Music

Hindustani Music

  • Vishnu Narayan Bhatkhande → He categorised ragas into 10 basic musical scales called Thaats.
  • Vishnu Digambar Paluskar → He founded Gandharva Mahavidyalaya (1901, Lahore).
  • There are 7 basic Talams in Carnatic music.

Carnatic Music

  • Purandar Das → He is considered as the Father of Carnatic Music.
  • M. S. Subbulakshmi → She is known as the Queen of Carnatic Music.
  • "Trinity of Carnatic Music" (also known as "Three Jewels of Carnatic Music") (18th Century) → Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar, and Syama Sastri.
  • M. S. Subbulakshmi was the first musician to receive Bharat Ratna in 1998.

§ 4Gharanas (School of Music)

Gwalior Gharana

  • It is considered as the oldest and most influential Khyal Gharana in Indian classical music.
  • It is said to have emerged during the reign of Mughal Emperor → Akbar (16th Century).
  • Ramtanu Pandey, later known as "Miyan Tansen" was one of the first and most famous vocalists of this Gharana (Akbar gave the honorific title "Miyan" to him).
  • Founders: Hassu Khan, Haddu Khan & Nathoo Khan, Nathan Pir Baksh.
  • Exponents: Raja Bhaiya Poonchhwale, Krishnarao Shankar, Pt. Omkarnath Thakur, Veena Sahasrabuddhe, Vishnu Digambar Paluskar, Bade Mohammad Khan.
  • Gwalior Gharana contemporary artist Sharad Sathe performing.
  • Tansen initially served in the court of Raja Ramchandra Singh of Rewa.
  • Guru of Tansen: Saint Haridas (he started Dagar Gharana).

§ 5Major Gharanas

Kirana Gharana (Uttar Pradesh)

  • This Gharana is known for its perfect note rendition (Sargam).
  • Founders: Abdul Karim Khan and Abdul Wahid Khan.
  • Exponents: Pt. Bhimsen Joshi (from Karnataka)
  • He received: Bharat Ratna (2008), Padma Vibhushan (1999), and Padma Bhushan (1985).
  • Sawai Gandharva (Guru of Pt. Bhimsen Joshi), Gangubai Hangal, Prabha Atre, Manik Varma, Chhanmull Mishra.

Kumara Gandharva (from Karnataka)

  • Original name: Shivaputra Siddaramaiah Komkalimath.
  • He refused to be associated with any Gharana.

Patiala Gharana

  • It was inspired and influenced by four Gharanas: Delhi, Rewa, Gwalior, Jaipur Gharanas.
  • This Gharana is known for its Ghazal, Khayal, and Thumri styles.
  • Founder: Mian Kallu (he played Sarangi).
  • Propounded by: Ustad Bade Fateh Ali Khan and Ustad Ali Baksh Jarnail Khan.
  • Exponents: Bade Ghulam Ali Khan, Begum Akhtar, Ajay Chakraborty, Naina Devi, Parveen Sultana, Lakshmi Shankar, Amanat Ali Khan.

Mewati Gharana (Haryana)

  • This Gharana is known for Tarana form of singing.
  • Founder: Ghagge Nazir Khan.
  • Exponents: Pt. Jasraj
  • He introduced Jugalbandi form of singing (Padma Vibhushan in 2000).
  • Maniram, Kala Ramnath (associated with Violin), Tripti Mukherjee, Ratan Mohan Sharma, Arvind Thatte.

Maihar Gharana

  • Founder: Ustad Allauddin Khan.
  • Unique feature: This Gharana is known for its blending of Hindustani and Carnatic elements, as well as its influence on Western music.
  • Exponents: Annapurna Devi
  • She plays surbahar and is daughter of Allaudin Khan.
  • She is the founder of Seni Gharana.
  • Ravi Shankar (Sitar), Nikhil Banerjee (Sitar), Ali Akbar Khan (Sarod and is son of Allaudin Khan), Hariprasad Chaurasia (Flute), Pannalal Ghosh (Flute), V G Jog (Violin).

Indore Gharana

  • Founder: Ustad Amir Khan.
  • Exponents: Sultan Khan (plays Sarangi), Pt. Amarnath, Shankar Lal Mishra, Kalyan Banerjee, Purabi Mukherjee.

Jaipur Atrauli Gharana

  • Founder: Alladiya Khan (he was from Aligarh then migrated to Jaipur).
  • Exponents: Kesarbai Kerkar, Mallikarjun Mansur, Vidyadhar Vyas, Bande Ali Khan (Rudra Veena), Pt. Lakshman Prasad, Kishori Amonkar.

Punjab Gharana

  • Founder: Lal Bhatwani Singh.
  • Exponents: Alla Rakha (Guru and father of Zakir Hussain), Zakir Hussain (he received Padma Vibhushan (2023)) → Both are Tabla player, Nikhil Ghosh (Tabla), Shafaat Ahmed Khan, Ustad Ashfaque Hussain, Miyan Qadir Baksh.

Benaras Gharana of Khayal

  • Founder: Pt. Gopal Mishra.

Benaras Gharana of Tabla

  • Founder: Pt. Ram Sahai.
  • Exponents: Ustad Bismilla Khan (plays Shehnai; received Bharat Ratna in 2001), Pt. Anokhelal Mishra (Tabla), Pt. Kishan Maharaj, Samta Prasad, Pt. Kanthe Maharaj, Gopal Mishra, Hanuman Prasad Mishra.

Rampur Sehaswan Gharana (Uttar Pradesh)

  • Founders: Ustad Inayat Khan and Mahbub Khan.
  • Exponents: Ghulam Mustafa Khan, Ustad Rashid Khan, Sadik Hussain Khan, Ustad Nisar Khan, Zeeshan Khan, Abbas Khan.

Bhendi Bazar Gharana (Mumbai)

  • Founder: Ustad Chhajju Khan (Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh).

§ 6Major Gharanas (continued)

  • Exponents: Aman Ali Khan, Lata Mangeshkar, Anjanibai Malpekar, Shashikala Koratkar.
  • Lata Mangeshkar: Bharat Ratna 2001, Padma Vibhushan 1999, Padma Bhushan 1969, Dada Saheb Phalke Award 1989.

Agra Gharana

  • This Gharana is known for its blend of Khayal and Dhrupad-Dhamar styles.
  • They are descendants of Nauhar Bani.
  • Founders: Haji Sujan Khan.
  • Exponents: Faiyaz Khan, Malka Jaan, Latafat Hussain Khan, Dinkar Kaikini, Vijay Kichlu, Lalita Rao, Ghagge Khuda Baksh.

Delhi Gharana

  • Founder: Sidhar Khan Dhadi.
  • Exponent: Tanras Khan.

Darbhanga Gharana (Bihar)

  • They sing Khandar Vani and Gauhar Vani forms of singing.
  • Founder: Radha Krishna and Karta Ram.
  • Exponents: Ram Chatur Mallick, Premkumar Mallick, Siyaram Tiwari, Vidur Mallick.

Dumrao Gharana

  • Founder: Pt. Ghanarang Baba.
  • Exponents: Pt. Tilak Chand Dubey, Ramjee Mishra.

Dagar Gharana

  • This Gharana is famous for its Dhrupad styles.
  • Exponents: Gundecha Brothers (Padma Shri in 2012), Zia Mohiuddin Dagar (Rudra Veena).
  • A distinct "dhrupad style" is associated with Bishnupur Gharana.

§ 7Gharanas of Kathak Dance

Lucknow Gharana of Kathak

  • Founder: Ishwari Prasad.
  • Exponents: Pandit Birju Maharaj, Shambhu Maharaj, Lacchu Maharaj, Kalika Prasad, Manjari Chaturvedi.

Benaras Gharana of Kathak (Uttar Pradesh)

  • Founder: Janaki Prasad.

Jaipur Gharana of Kathak

  • Founder: Bhanu Ji Maharaj.
  • Exponent: Vidyagauri Adkar.

Raigarh Gharana of Kathak

  • Founder: Raja Chakradhar Singh.
  • (A) Pt. Birju Maharaj; (B) Janaki Prasad; (C) Raja Chakradhar Singh.

Wanawun music is sung in wedding ceremonies in J&K.

§ 8Key concepts

  • Hindustani vs Carnatic Music – regions, languages, common elements (Raga, Taal, Sruti)

  • Gharana of Kathak – Lucknow, Benaras, Jaipur, Raigarh
